$comment: Tier-2 DB-state fixture spec for W4.6b — the conversation-summary vault mirror
+ delete sweep (v4 lib/file-storage/conversation-summary-vault-bridge.ts, driven
through repos.chats.delete(id, { syncVaults }) for the sweep). One committed file
drives BOTH sides:
- the v4 oracle (build-vault-summary-mirror-fixture.ts + vault-summary-mirror-tier2.ts)
- the Rust port (quilltap-harness vault_summary_mirror_tier2 test).
FIXTURE: TWO characters WITH vaults (via v4's REAL repos.characters.create, pinned
ids + full vault provisioning) and TWO chats (via repos.chats.create, pinned ids +
timestamps), each chat carrying BOTH characters as CHARACTER participants (one
llm-, one user-controlled). chat_messages is materialized (getMessageCount) so the
Rust delete's clear_messages has a table. All mount-index store tables + doc_mount_chunks
are materialized via generateDDL so v4's post-write reindexSingleFile runs cleanly.
OPS (all fields PINNED — every timestamp / generation is caller-supplied, so the
authored file bytes are byte-identical on both sides, no minted timestamp in content):
1. write chat1 'Title A' gen1 -> both vaults get 'Conversation Summaries/Title A.md'.
2. write chat1 'Title B' gen2 -> rename-by-UUID: prior 'Title A.md' (same
conversationId) deleted, 'Title B.md' written (proves idempotency + rename).
3. write chat2 'Other' -> a distinct conversation's file in both vaults.
4. repos.chats.delete(chat1, { syncVaults: true })  -> chat1's summary swept
from both vaults; chat2's remains.
5. repos.chats.delete(chat2, { syncVaults: false }) -> chat2's summary files REMAIN.
DUMP: the five mount-index store tables (doc_mount_points / doc_mount_folders /
doc_mount_files / doc_mount_documents / doc_mount_file_links). doc_mount_documents.content
is diffed byte-for-byte (deterministic — all input timestamps pinned).
NORMALIZATION: minted-values remap with ONE shared id-map across the five tables
(points -> folders -> files -> documents -> links, rows in natural-key order). Every
mount-index row id is minted (vault provisioning + the summary writes), so FKs verify
by relationship. Timestamps -> <ts>; the link chunkCount -> <cc> (a v4-only
reindexSingleFile artifact — the Rust storage primitive does not chunk); doc_mount_chunks
is excluded. Character/chat ids are PINNED, so they appear literally (identical both
sides) inside the frontmatter content and are NOT remapped.
SAFETY: testPepperBase64 is a THROWAWAY 32-byte key (the same one folders/tags/
characters-create use). NOT the real Friday pepper; safe to commit.
